translations.text: Simon Peter, a servant and apostle of Jesus Christ, to those who have received faith equal in honor to ours through the righteousness of our God and Savior Jesus Christ.
May grace and peace be multiplied to you through the knowledge of God and of Jesus Christ our Lord.
Since his divine power has granted us everything needed for life and devotion to God, through the knowledge of the one who called us into his own glory and splendor,
through these he has given us the greatest and most precious promises, so that through them you may share in the divine nature, having escaped the desires of this world and its corruption.
For this very reason, make every effort to supply virtue with your faith, and knowledge with virtue,
and self-control with knowledge, and endurance with self-control, and devotion to God with endurance,
and brotherly affection with devotion to God, and love with brotherly affection.
If you possess these things and increase in them, they will keep you from being idle and unfruitful in the knowledge of our Lord Jesus Christ.
But anyone who lacks these things is nearly blind and shortsighted, having forgotten the cleansing of his former sins.
Therefore, brothers, strive all the more to keep your calling and election secure through good works. If you do these things, you will never stumble.
For in this way entrance into the eternal kingdom of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ will be richly granted to you.
Therefore I will always be ready to remind you of these things, even though you know them and are established in the truth that has reached you.
For I consider it right, as long as I am here in the body, to awaken you with reminders.
I know that I will very soon be stripped of this body, as our Lord Jesus Christ has shown me.
And I eagerly strive always to encourage you, so that even after my departure from this world you will remember these things.
For we did not follow cleverly embellished tales when we made known to you the power and coming of our Lord Jesus Christ, but we ourselves were eyewitnesses of his majesty.
For he received glory and honor from God the Father when this voice came to him from the magnificent glory: “This is my beloved Son, with whom I am pleased.”
We ourselves heard this voice coming from heaven when we were with him on the holy mountain.
And we have the prophetic word made more certain. You do well to heed it as a lamp that gives light in a dark place, until the day grows bright and the morning star rises in your hearts.
But know this first: no prophecy of Scripture has its own interpretation.
For prophecy was never given according to human will, but people spoke from God as they were carried along by the Holy Spirit.

There were also false prophets among the people, just as there will now be false teachers among you. They will secretly introduce destructive heresies and, denying the Lord who bought them, bring swift destruction upon themselves.
Many will fall into following their immoral ways, and because of them the way of truth will be reviled.
In their greed they will make merchandise of you with fabricated words. Their judgment, pronounced long ago, is not idle, and their destruction does not sleep.
For if God did not spare the angels who sinned, but cast them into Tartarus in chains of darkness and handed them over to be kept for judgment,
He did not spare the world at the beginning either, but preserved Noah, the eighth person, a preacher of righteousness, from the flood he brought upon the world of the ungodly.
And he condemned the cities of Sodom and Gomorrah, reducing them to ashes and making them an example for those who would afterward live ungodly lives.
And he rescued righteous Lot, who was distressed by lawless, lustful conduct.
For that righteous man, living among them and seeing and hearing what they did, tormented his own holy soul day after day because of their lawless conduct.
The Lord knows how to rescue the godly from temptation and to keep the unrighteous under punishment for the day of judgment,
especially those who follow the flesh in defiling desires and despise authority. Brazen and audacious, they do not hesitate to blaspheme glorious beings,
whereas angels, greater than they in strength and power, do not bring a slanderous judgment against them from the Lord.
But these people, like speechless animals destined by their natural instincts for destruction and decay, blaspheme what they do not understand, and will perish in their own corruption.
They suffer punishment as the wages of unrighteousness. They consider indulgence during the day a delight. They are spots and blemishes, indulging in their own deceptions while feasting with you.
They have eyes like those of prostitutes, never ceasing from sin. They entice unstable souls and have hearts trained in greed. They are children of a curse.
Leaving the straight path, they went astray, following the path of Balaam, son of Beor, and loved the wages of unrighteousness.
He received a rebuke for his own lawlessness: the speechless donkey spoke with a human voice and restrained the prophet’s lawlessness.
Such people are springs without water and mists driven by a storm. The gloom of darkness is reserved for them forever.
For, speaking boastful words of emptiness, they entice through sensuality and fleshly desires those who truly escape from people who live in error.
They promise them freedom, while they themselves are slaves of corruption, for whatever overcomes a person also enslaves that person.

For if, after escaping the defilements of the world through the knowledge of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ, they become entangled in them again and are overcome, their final condition has become worse than their first.
For it would have been better for them never to have known the way of righteousness than to have known it and then turned back from the holy commandment handed down to them.
The true proverb of admonition has come to apply to them: “A dog returns to its own vomit,” and, “A washed pig rolls in the mud.”
Beloved, I am writing this second letter to you, in which I stir your steadfast minds by way of reminder.
To remember the words previously spoken by the holy prophets and the commands of the Lord and Savior given by your apostles.
But know this first: in the last days contemptuous mockers will come, living according to their own desires.
They will say, “Where is the promise of his coming? For ever since the fathers fell asleep, everything remains just as it was from the beginning of creation.”
For those who desire this forget that the heavens existed from the beginning, and that the earth came from the waters and the waters stand established by the word of God.
Because of this, the world that then existed was destroyed and perished in a flood.
But the present heavens and earth are stored up by the same word for fire, kept for the day of judgment and the destruction of ungodly people.
And do not let this escape you, beloved: one day with the Lord is like a thousand years, and a thousand years like one day.
The Lord does not delay his promise, as some consider it a delay, but is patient with you, because he does not want anyone to perish, but wants everyone to come to repentance.

But the day of the Lord will come like a thief. On that day the heavens will pass away with a tumult, the elements will be burned and dissolved by fire, and the earth and all the works in it will be found.
Since all these things are to be dissolved in this way, what kind of people ought you to be, looking forward with holy and godly conduct
and hastening toward the coming of the day of the Lord, when the heavens will be set ablaze and dissolved, and the elements will burn and melt?
In accordance with the promises, we look forward to and await new heavens and a new earth, in which righteousness dwells.
Therefore, beloved, as you await these things, be diligent to be found by him spotless and blameless, in peace.
And regard the Lord’s patience as salvation, just as our beloved brother Paul also wrote to you according to the wisdom granted to him by God.

He also speaks about these things in all his letters. In them are some things that are difficult to understand, which the unlearned and unstable twist, as they do all the Scriptures, to their own destruction.
You, therefore, beloved, knowing this beforehand, be on your guard so that you are not carried away by the error of the lawless and fall from your firm footing.
Grow in the grace and knowledge of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ. To him be glory both now and on the day of eternity. Amen.
